Hi Laura,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement asked me to get the insurance evidence aligned before we sign the MSA/order form for the pilot. Attached is the carrier's preliminary COI and policy schedule — insurer says they can issue a standard COI but have questions about the Additional Insured (AI) language in your MSA redlines.

Quick asks:
- Can Redwood accept the carrier's AI waiver instead of naming Redwood as "Additional Insured" on the policy?
- Are the coverage minimums below (Cyber E&O $3M / GL $2M / Auto $1M / Umbrella $5M) sufficient for your compliance gate?
- If a retro-date or retro policy endorsement is required, what is the acceptable window?

I've attached the COI draft and the broker's LOI. We need a short playbook so our legal + broker can finalize documents this week.

Best,
Alyssa

Subject: Re: Insurance and COI for pilot — next steps

Alyssa — thanks, and appreciate you sending the draft COI. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and David (risk) to confirm acceptance criteria.

High level from our side:
- We prefer being named as Additional Insured when possible. If the carrier refuses that form of endorsement, a written waiver/endorsement confirming no subrogation and primary/non-contributory status may be acceptable, but we'd need explicit language and insurer-to-insurer confirmation.
- Coverage minimums you listed are reasonable starting points; Kimberly, please confirm if Cyber E&O $3M is acceptable for the pilot or whether we should require $5M.
- Retro-dates: for pilot engagements we ask for either an endorsement covering the effective date of the order form or a retroactive date not earlier than 30 days before signing.

Action items:
1) Kimberly — review attached COI and advise on AI/waiver acceptability + any draft wording we should propose to the broker.
2) Ben — can you push the insurer for a carrier-letter or specific endorsement text rather than broker language?
3) Alyssa — if procurement needs a temporary exception to close, let us know timeline and we can propose a documented mitigation plan.

Attaching our annotated MSA redlines to help: MSA_redlines_202608.pdf

Thanks — Laura

[attachment: MSA_redlines_202608.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, Alyssa Perez <alyssa.perez@bluehaven.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Insurance and COI for pilot — next steps

Thanks Laura. I reviewed the COI and Bluehaven's broker note. Summary and recommended path:

Summary:
- COI reflects the carrier's limits: GL $2M, Cyber E&O $3M, Umbrella $5M, Auto $1M. Endorsement language for AI is not present on the COI; broker indicates the carrier can add an AI endorsement but prefers a waiver for administrative simplicity.

Recommendations:
1) Additional Insured: we should request the "CG 20 10" series or equivalent ISO Additional Insured endorsement on the GL policy limited to liability arising out of Bluehaven's work for Redwood. If carrier flatly refuses, accept a signed insurer letter confirming: (a) Redwood is treated as Additional Insured for claims arising from Bluehaven's work; and (b) the AI protection is primary and non-contributory.

2) Cyber E&O: for a pilot that will process PII and customer prompts, bump to $5M if possible. If broker cannot secure $5M within the procurement timeline, allow $3M with compensating controls and a shorter exception window.

3) Retro-date: Acceptable retro is up to 30 days prior to effective date. If the carrier can only provide an endorsement with a retro longer than 30 days, require a written attestation explaining the gap and mitigation steps.

Suggested language for broker to push (copy/paste):
"The insurer will add Redwood Inference, Inc. as an Additional Insured on the Commercial General Liability policy (form CG 20 10 or equivalent), limited to liability arising out of the operations of the Named Insured (Bluehaven Tech) performed on behalf of Redwood Inference, Inc., and shall be primary and non-contributory with respect to any insured loss; waiver of subrogation as to Redwood Inference, Inc. is also granted where permitted by law."

If Bluehaven needs a sign-off timeline, we can accept a documented temporary exception for up to 45 days provided: (a) a current COI is delivered; (b) broker provides a firm schedule to obtain AI endorsement; and (c) we get a risk acceptance memo signed by David.

-Kimberly

[inline: suggested endorsement wording]

From: Ben Ross <ben.ross@oakridge-brokers.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Alyssa Perez <alyssa.perez@bluehaven.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Insurance and COI for pilot — next steps

Laura/Kimberly — thanks for the clear guidance. Quick status from carrier: they can add the AI endorsement but charge an additional premium. The carrier underwriting team is pushing back on the Cyber E&O $5M at the moment due to Bluehaven's revenue profile; $3M is the appetite today.

Two possible paths and timeframes:
A) AI endorsement added to GL + written confirmation of primary/non-contributory — estimated 7–10 business days after we submit the endorsement request (carrier process).
B) Immediate close with temporary exception: broker letter + COI (what Alyssa shared) while we secure endorsement. Broker can provide a binding timeline for endorsement within 30 days, but the carrier expects an additional premium for AI and may require a simple policy change.

I've attached a short LOI and the broker's recommended exception wording. If Redwood accepts a 30–45 day temporary exception (with a signed risk memo), we can close quickly and then finalize endorsement.

[attachment: Broker_Letter_of_Intent.docx (DOCX, 22KB)]

-Ben

Team — I reviewed Kimberly's suggestion and Ben's timing. Risk acceptance parameters I can sign off on (internal) for a temporary exception up to 45 days provided the following are delivered and approved:
1) Current COI on file showing limits (already provided).
2) Broker-provided signed LOI with timeline to obtain AI endorsement (<= 30 days preferred).
3) Compensating controls checklist from Bluehaven (access controls, data retention policy, SOC 2 in progress) — link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xY_bluehaven_evidence
4) Executive sign-off from Bluehaven procurement acknowledging the exception and agreeing to the endorsement timeline.

If the cyber limit stays at $3M, we require the compensating controls documentation and accelerated notification commitments in the order form (72-hour breach notice).

If above are in place, I will produce a risk acceptance memo and sign it. Laura — you can proceed to close under those conditions.

-David
